_comment: iter-106 WER fixture corpus. Each entry pairs a hand-curated
reference (the ground-truth transcript) with a simulated STT
hypothesis that exercises a specific error pattern. The
expected_wer_min/max bounds are tight enough to catch a
regression in the compute_wer primitive but loose enough to
survive the natural rounding of the (S+D+I)/N formula.
When a real CPU-only STT lands (faster-whisper, whisper.cpp
wrapper, etc.), the integration test can swap the simulated
hypothesis for the STT output and the same expected ranges
still apply — production-grade STT lands in 0.0-0.2 WER on
entries simulate degraded conditions that real audio fixtures
would need separate noisy-mic recordings to reproduce.

fixtures.name: clean
fixtures.description: Perfect transcription — production-grade STT on clean audio.

fixtures.name: dropped_filler
fixtures.description: STT drops the leading filler 'um' — common.
fixtures.reference: um what is the weather today

fixtures.name: noisy
fixtures.reference: the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog
fixtures.hypothesis: the quick crown fox jumped on the lazy dog

fixtures.name: catastrophic
fixtures.description: STT misheard the entire utterance — every word wrong.
